blocks.title: Dative bond
blocks.text: A dative bond is formed between two atoms when the shared pair of electrons is donated by one of the bonding atoms.

Consider the bond formation between H2O and a proton H+. Water has two covalent bonds and two lone pairs of electrons on the oxygen atom; the proton is deficient in electrons. The oxygen atom can therefore donate one lone pair to the acceptor H+, which results in a dative bond and the oxonium (hydronium) ion H3O+. Carbon monoxide also contains a dative bond between oxygen and carbon. Oxygen shares two valence electrons with carbon to make a normal double covalent bond, but the valency of carbon is not satisfied by these bonds; it needs one more pair to complete its octet, and oxygen donates one of its lone pairs to form a covalent bond that is a dative bond.

Ozone is formed by a reaction between an oxygen molecule and an oxygen atom, a free radical. One of the oxygen atoms of the molecule donates a pair of electrons to make a coordinate covalent bond with this free radical, so the central atom has three bonds in all, a double covalent bond on one side and a coordinate covalent bond on the other. The central atom carries a positive charge, while the oxygen atom that accepts the lone pair carries a negative charge.

blocks.prompt: Boron in BF3 has six valence electrons around it. Show how a dative bond forms between NH3 and BF3, and say which atom is the donor.
blocks.explanation: Nitrogen in NH3 has a lone pair; boron in BF3 has only three bond pairs, six electrons, and an empty orbital able to accept two more. The nitrogen lone pair is donated into boron's empty orbital, giving the dative bond H3N to BF3; nitrogen is the donor and boron the acceptor, and both now have an octet.

items: Dative (coordinate covalent) bond: both shared electrons come from one atom. H3O+ (O lone pair to H+), CO (O lone pair to C beside the double bond), O3 (one O of O2 donates to the oxygen free radical; central O +, acceptor O -).
